fact_text: Retail and wholesale trade makes a large contribution to Pakistan's GDP, the interviewee said, and organised tier-one retail chains are a key part of that trade.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: Organised tier-one retail, meaning chains with several outlets in different cities, accounts for about 10 percent of Pakistan's retail trade, and the rest is undocumented or unorganised.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said organised retail is about 15 to 25 percent of trade in neighbouring countries, so Pakistan's organised share lags its neighbours by a wide margin.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: All tier-one retail transactions are reported to the FBR through point-of-sale systems, and an economic survey cited in the interview recorded documented retail sales of PKR 2.9 trillion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said tier-one retailers operate under a separate tax regime created by law, so the documented tenth of retail carries most of the tax load while the other 90 percent is taxed differently.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee estimated that sales tax and income tax together make up about 20 to 25 percent of a tier-one product's selling price.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: Buying scale lets a large tier-one retailer offset only about 5 to 10 percent of the 20 to 25 percent tax load, the interviewee said, leaving a cost gap against untaxed sellers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee argued that customers shift to cheaper goods, so a tax-heavy documented segment loses share to untaxed sellers whose prices carry less tax.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: Tier-one retailers deal with about 50 to 60 regulators, the interviewee said, with two to three demands each month, so many firms must hire separate staff just for tax and compliance.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: Retail plans about six months ahead for design, production and stock, so a sudden 25 to 40 percent fall in volume from policy leaves rent and wages unchanged and can wipe out the business.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: Retail closing hours were restricted from 7 April 2026, first to 8 p.m. and later eased to 9 p.m. in Punjab and Islamabad, which Balochistan also adopted, while Sindh did not.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the austerity measures have been lifted, including the government's own, but shop closing hours remain restricted, with some shops shut at 9 p.m. while restaurants may open until 11 p.m.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee called the uneven closing rules discriminatory, since shops in malls and prominent markets close early while other outlets are exempt, which undermines a level playing field.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: At the 8 p.m. closing time, the interviewee said retail, manufacturing and services together lost about PKR 100 billion of economic activity a week, about 60 percent of it manufacturing-linked.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: At the 8 p.m. closing time the weekly tax loss was up to PKR 25 billion, the interviewee said, including sales tax at 18 percent on the goods not sold.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: After the closing time was eased to 9 p.m., the interviewee put the weekly economic loss at about PKR 15 to 20 billion, with a weekly tax loss of about PKR 4 to 5 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said about 15 percent of local manufacturing is hit by the closing hours, with factories cutting from double shifts to single or one-and-a-half shifts and some staff laid off.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: Fewer working hours in retail and manufacturing cut incomes and slow the economy, the interviewee argued, and he said the closing-hour restrictions may be made permanent, leaving firms no option but to keep staff cuts.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The retail body asked for a closing time of at least 10 p.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m. at weekends, arguing that 9 p.m. closing makes little sense for commuting workers and families.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The retail body asked the government to reintroduce daylight saving time by advancing clocks in summer, a step the interviewee said the economy had tried before and should reconsider.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The retail body asked that compliant tier-one shops in malls and markets not be forced to close early, arguing that matching closing times is at least a level playing field if tax parity is not possible.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The Third Schedule, meant for standardised goods such as soap and shampoo taxed at factory price, was extended to footwear, leather goods, bags, backpacks and children's items; clothing was not added.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: A retailer that designs, sources, prices and sells its own goods still pays the Third Schedule tax on the full price, even though its transactions are already reported through point-of-sale systems.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: With 18 percent GST charged on the full price, a 30 percent seasonal discount lifts the effective tax to about 26 percent and a 50 percent discount to about 36 percent of the discounted price.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee estimated that items moved to the Third Schedule would carry an effective tax of about 22 to 30 percent, against the 18 percent GST, making them dearer for customers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: During budget discussions, tax officials themselves acknowledged that the Third Schedule extension would make these goods more expensive, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The retail body argued that a Third Schedule levy on top of GST for compliant retailers, whose transactions are already reported, would feed inflation and penalise the documented sector.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: Some Pakistani brands, mainly women's clothing labels, have opened stores abroad in the UK, the USA, the Middle East and Bangladesh, and also sell through e-commerce to overseas Pakistanis.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said overseas expansion is a first step, since locations, laws, regulations and staffing abroad differ from Pakistan, and brands must first thrive at home before expanding.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)

fact_text: Pakistani western-wear, footwear and electronics brands that have begun local manufacturing could add to exports if the domestic market lets them grow, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Aren't Pakistani Brands Global? The Challenges Holding Back Retail Industry | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-07-10)
